tables.title: Effect of low-power modes to I2C
tables.text: Table 420, "Effect of low-power modes to I2C", in section 41.5 (I2C in low-power modes) on page 1671. Columns: Mode, Description. 3 data row(s). Notes: 1. Refer to Section41.3: I2C implementation for information about the Stop modes supported by each instance. If the wake-up from a specific stop mode is not supported, the instance must be disabled be.

rows: No effect. I2C interrupts cause the device to exit the Sleep mode.

The contents of I2C registers are kept.
–WUPEN = 1 and I2C is clocked by an internal oscillator (HSI). The address recognition 
is functional. The I2C address match condition causes the device to exit the Stop mode.
–WUPEN = 0: I2C must be disabled before entering Stop mode.
The I2C peripheral is powered down. It must be reinitialized after exiting Standby mode.
notes: 1. Refer to Section41.3: I2C implementation for information about the Stop modes supported by each instance. If the wake-up from a specific stop mode is not supported, the instance must be disabled before entering that specific Stop mode.
